item.title: Hershey Defeats Reese’s Lawsuit Over Halloween Pumpkins That Lacked ‘Cool’ Carvings
item.description: Hershey won the dismissal of a lawsuit claiming it let down consumers because its Halloween-themed Reese’s pumpkins lacked the decorative carved designs shown on the packaging. “Plaintiffs do not allege that the Hershey’s Reese’s Peanut Butter Pumpkins that they purchased were defective or worthless or that they lost all economic value because of the absence of the decorative carvings.” The judge also said Vidal and Granados could not show they paid up to 25% too much by citing Reese’s prices at Target, at Walmart and in Hershey’s online store, because they bought their candy at a Publix supermarket. In a court filing seeking the lawsuit’s dismissal, Hershey said its packaging included a disclaimer that the depicted carvings were a “decorating suggestion.”

item.title: White House Weighs US Incubator for Cyber Research, Startups
item.description: The White House’s Office of the National Cyber Director has been drafting an executive order that would establish a program to research and develop cyber technologies that are aligned with the priorities of the U.S. The Trump administration is weighing a plan to establish a government-led incubator aimed at investing in cybersecurity research and spinning out startups focused on developing tools for the government to use, according to people familiar with the situation. government, the effort has been compared with the way Israel closely aligns its military priorities with the focus of cybersecurity startups, venture capital investments and academic research in the country, according to the people familiar with the plans.

item.title: Satellites Show Earth Lost More Than 12T Tons of Ice in 47 Years
item.description: About 12.5 trillion tons (11.3 trillion metric tons) of ice from glaciers in Greenland and Antarctica have melted since 1979, which is enough frozen water to stack ice 5 feet (1.5 meters) deep across the continental United States, according to a major scientific report. A warming Earth is accelerating the melting of the planet’s two major ice sheets, with five-sixths of the melt not coming from hotter air, but from warmer waters eating away at the ice sheets from below and the sides, with glaciers flowing into the oceans, according to a study in Wednesday’s journal Scientific Data. But by incorporating NASA satellites, the scientists were able to chart ice sheet volumes in Antarctica back to 1979 and in Greenland back to 1972.

item.title: UK Insurers Urge Bank of England to Rethink ‘Dynamic’ Stress Test
item.description: Britain’s insurance industry is urging the Bank of England’s regulatory arm to rethink its live crisis simulation, citing heavy reporting demands and unrealistic scenarios in a stress test that pushed firms “to their absolute limit.” The Prudential Regulation Authority’s first “dynamic” stress test, which ran over three weeks in May, subjected insurers to successive crises including a U.S. Unlike previous stress tests that assessed how insurers would handle predefined shocks, this one – known as DyGIST – tested insurers’ ability to respond in real time to adverse conditions as they unfold, with scenario details revealed only during the live exercise. “The accumulation of scenarios in such a short time frame was very unlikely,” said Nafisah Hussain, director of public policy at the International Underwriting Association, a trade body for insurers and reinsurers in the London market that has fed its views back to the PRA.

item.title: FDA Declares Cyclospora Outbreak Over
item.description: The Cyclospora outbreak that impacted people in more than 21 states has been declared over by the U.S. Though the outbreak is over, the FDA continues the outbreak investigation of Cyclospora infections linked to iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico and recalled by Taylor Farms de Mexico. Since the last update on August 27, 2026, state and local health officials have continued to interview additional sick people with Cyclosporiasis and the CDC has added them to this multi-state outbreak.

item.title: Pillar Capital Management adopts Ultrassure to support contract review workflows
item.description: Pillar Capital Management, the Bermuda-based specialist collateralized reinsurance and insurance-linked securities (ILS) investment manager, has adopted Ultrassure, an AI contract intelligence platform for insurance and reinsurance, to support its contract review and underwriting workflows. Pillar selected Ultrassure to enhance its contract review workflows after completing a comprehensive evaluation of the platform. Jeff Franklin, Chief Underwriting Officer at Pillar Capital Management, commented: “Ultrassure demonstrated a strong understanding of the reinsurance business and was responsive to our feedback on the platform throughout the process.” Matti Parnanen, Founder and CEO of Ultrassure, said: “We have enjoyed working with the Pillar team and appreciate the thoughtful feedback they provided during the evaluation.

item.title: Busy August pushes Allstate’s current aggregate year pre-tax cat losses to $3.15bn
item.description: A busy August in catastrophe loss terms from severe weather activity has resulted in large US insurer Allstate reporting $748 million in pre-tax losses, which has lifted the total across the current annual aggregate risk period for its catastrophe bonds to $3.15 billion so far. July and August were particularly busy months in catastrophe loss terms for Allstate, with the two-month period generating a combined $1.43 billion in pre-tax losses, or $1.13 billion, after-tax Allstate currently has annual aggregate protection from only one cat bond tranche, the $150 million Class B tranche of notes issued through its Sanders Re III Ltd. This remains a notably heavy start to the annual aggregate year for Allstate’s pre-tax overall catastrophe losses.

item.description: injury law firm with offices in all states, plans to spend $1 billion on artificial intelligence and other legal technology over the next decade. Morgan said the platform now has almost 5,000 regular users.

item.title: EPIC Acquires Michigan’s Korotkin Insurance Group
item.description: EPIC Insurance Brokers & Consultants has acquired Korotkin Insurance Group, a fifth-generation independent brokerage with over a century of operational history in Michigan. KIG brings a strong regional presence and specialized expertise across multiple industries and client segments to EPIC’s growing national platform. Grand Rapids based-KIG will serve as a key anchor for the firm’s continued growth in Michigan and the broader region.

item.title: People Moves: Alliant Adds Bryant to Employee Benefits Group in Texas
item.description: Alliant Insurance Services has hired Jennifer Bryan t as senior vice president within its employee benefits group, based in Dallas, Texas. Bryant will work with employers to develop strategic health and welfare solutions while building long-term relationships and connecting clients with the resources needed to address evolving benefits challenges. Bryson brings more than 20 years of experience in employee benefits, health and welfare consulting, business development, and client relationship management.

item.title: Sompo International hires Nicolas Berg to head UK Insurance business
item.description: Sompo International has appointed Nicolas (Nic) Berg as chief executive officer of its UK Insurance business, succeeding Sarah Stanford, who is stepping down after leading the business through the initial integration period following Sompo’s acquisition of Aspen. He joins Sompo from SCOR Group, where he most recently served as chief executive officer of SCOR US and head of P&C North America. In his new role, Berg will be based in London and report to Alessa Quane, chief executive officer of International Markets.

item.title: Jensten Group to acquire technology-focused corporate broker Venture Risks Group
item.description: Jensten Group has agreed to acquire Venture Risks Group (VRG), a specialist technology-focused corporate broker, as it looks to expand its presence in the technology and life sciences sectors. The transaction, which is expected to complete in October 2026, will further strengthen Jensten Group’s technology, media, cyber, and life sciences division. It will also enhance the group’s specialist capabilities across professional indemnity, cyber, and technology-related risks.

item.title: Earnix pushes insurance AI from advice into action with Agent Hub launch
item.description: Earnix, a Boston-headquartered insurtech, has launched Agent Hub, bringing more than 25 insurance-specific AI agents and apps into its AI Orchestration System (AIOS). The new catalogue brings agentic AI directly into Earnix’s pricing and rating, underwriting, and customer engagement solutions. As AI increases the speed and scope of what insurers can analyse and recommend, Earnix argues that the next step is enabling intelligence to operate within the business processes where those decisions are made, while maintaining the governance and accountability required for high-stakes insurance activity.

item.title: Edmond de Rothschild Says Client Queries ‘Pouring in’ After Europe’s Wildfires
item.description: Edmond de Rothschild Group, the Swiss money manager, says it’s been fielding client inquiries since the summer amid concerns that Europe’s intensifying wildfire season represents a fundamental shift in how to view portfolio risk in the region. “Since our clientele is very European, questions have really been pouring in much more frequently since this summer — far more so than during the massive wildfires in Los Angeles.” De Tessieres says EdR now intends to conduct “more frequent portfolio valuations” to identify which holdings are most exposed. For example, one Europe-focused client “asked very specifically whether this has an impact on the valuations of her real estate portfolio, particularly on specific properties within her portfolio,” de Tessieres said in an interview.

item.title: Zillow Loses Antitrust Battle Over Chicago Area Listing Feed
item.description: Seattle-based Zillow previously won a court order that reinstated the Chicago-area listings after MRED cut off its data feed in May. in Chicago dissolved a previous order that required Midwest Real Estate Data, the multiple listings service for the Chicagoland area, to temporarily maintain Zillow’s access to listings. “If Zillow doesn’t enforce its listing ban, it will not lose access to the listing feeds and it can avoid any harm.” MRED said the decision reinforces the ability of listing services “to consistently enforce their rules and data licensing agreements.” In a statement on its website, Zillow said it was disappointed in the decision, which it called “a step back for Chicago home buyers and sellers.” The company said it will continue with the case as it moves into arbitration.

item.description: Source traceability in a medical chronology means every individual entry carries a citation: the name of the source document, the provider or facility, the date of service, and the specific page in the original record the entry was drawn from. It’s important to know whether every entry in the generated AI medical chronology can be traced back to a specific document, provider, date, and page in the original record set. item.title: FCA sets out steps to support small businesses' access to finance
item.description: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) could access finance more easily after the FCA sets out practical steps to help. As part of its commitment to supporting growth, the FCA is focusing its next steps in three areas to help reduce friction: Graeme Reynolds, FCA director of competition, said: 'Small businesses need to be able to access the finance they need at the right time to start up, grow and invest. We're focusing on where we can make a practical difference by reducing unnecessary friction, supporting a more proportionate regulatory framework and helping unlock the benefits of open finance.' item.title: FCA and partners continues crackdown on illegal crypto trading
item.description: The FCA and partners have taken further action against illegal peer-to-peer crypto trading in London. The FCA has carried out further operations with partners to disrupt illegal peer-to-peer crypto trading across multiple London locations. item.title: Property reinsurance investing offers more manageable tail risk than perceived: Agecroft
item.description: Amongst the primary benefits, Steinbrugge highlights how property reinsurance investments can offer a more attractive and manageable tail-risk profile than commonly perceived. While property reinsurance and insurance-linked investment strategies are often viewed as carrying significant tail risk, Agecroft Partners believes that carefully constructed portfolios and disciplined underwriting can help to manage downside volatility more effectively than headline risk profiles may suggest. Steinbrugge further added: “While property reinsurance is often viewed as carrying significant tail risk, carefully constructed portfolios and disciplined underwriting can potentially manage downside volatility more effectively than the headline risk profile might suggest.” In addition, the CEO affirms that property reinsurance can also offer modeled forward returns that outperform many traditional fixed-income strategies.

item.title: Climate, Seismic Factors Primed ‘Unprecedented’ Nepal Disaster
item.description: The catastrophic mountain flooding in Nepal that killed more than 1,300 people was driven by a complex web of climate and seismic processes that made it nearly impossible to predict, according to an international team of scientists. “This is an unprecedented disaster in the Himalayas,” said Walter Immerzeel, a mountain hydrologist at Utrecht University and co-author of the report, during a press briefing. Nepal has already sought compensation from the United Nations Fund for responding to Loss and Damage, a nascent climate-aid system set up to help developing nations deal with the worst impacts of global warming.

item.title: El Niño, War Raise Asia’s Food Security Risks, Verisk Maplecroft Says
item.description: Severe weather disruptions will amplify food security risks in Asia, potentially triggering civil unrest and political instability in vulnerable countries such as India, Indonesia and the Philippines, according to consultancy Verisk Maplecroft. Over half of countries that are at high- or very high-risk on Verisk Maplecroft’s Food Security Index also sit within the two highest categories of its predictive Civil Unrest Index. For conflict-stricken nations like Afghanistan and Myanmar, a food shock would raise the risk of a humanitarian catastrophe, it added.

item.title: Russia’s Attacks on Europe Are Getting More Brazen and More Dangerous
item.description: “As a company whose systems are used by several NATO member states and other ally and partner nations, including Ukraine, we need to take the resultant risks into account.” Read more: Europe Struggles to Counter Russian Attacks Falling Short of War Just this week, the US Justice Department accused the Russian intelligence service of “conspiring to finance terrorism and commit murder for hire” in Europe at the behest of the Kremlin. As Vladimir Putin’s war on Ukraine grinds on with little movement on the battlefield and thousands of casualties each week, so-called hybrid attacks on Europe are increasing not just in number, but in their recklessness. “We struggle to counter so-called hybrid attacks with open societies that make it easy for the attacker,” said James Everard, former NATO Deputy Supreme Allied Commander Europe.

item.title: Roost acquired; new owner discontinues Security360
item.description: The new owner has discontinued Roost’s Security360 and WS360 home-security products and associated monitoring services while apparently retaining Protection360, its commercial-property telematics product, which remains available on the company’s website. Roost Home Telematics was acquired by an undisclosed company at the end of August. The acquisition also ends Roost’s relationship with investor and insurance partner USAA , which primarily offered the Security360 solution.

item.title: Palette embeds fine-art transit insurance
item.description: Fine-art logistics platform Palette has partnered with Marsh to let users obtain insurance estimates and arrange specialist transit coverage directly through its platform. Palette said the insurance integration eliminates the need for separate communications and processes when arranging coverage for artwork in transit. The insurance program is led by AXA XL and integrates coverage into the same workflow customers use to request shipping estimates, select logistics providers and manage shipments.

item.title: Why Automation-First AI Falls Short in Specialty Lines
item.description: A system can identify every limit, exclusion and endorsement in a policy and still get the coverage analysis wrong. It may read every page yet miss how an endorsement changes the coverage grant, where an excess layer departs from the underlying coverage, or how the facts change a provision’s meaning. Coverage is a promise wrapped in documents.

item.title: Federal Legislation Targets Auto Insurance Fraud With Steep Penalties
item.description: The bipartisan bill, Stop Auto Fraud Act of 2026, targets deliberately staged accidents intended to defraud insurance companies, imposing stiff penalties, including possible jail time, for violations. Earlier this month, federal legislation was introduced to make motor vehicle collision fraud a federal crime, according to a joint press release by Congresswoman Laura Gillen (D-NY-04) alongside U.S Representatives Troy Nehls (R-TX-22), Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-05) and Vince Fong (R-CA-20). Long a target of fraudulent auto insurance claims, the commercial trucking industry also welcomed the legislation.

item.title: Data centre build-out will force industry to rethink approaches to risk modeling: Arbol CEO
item.description: As billions of dollars continue to flow into new infrastructure such as AI data centres, the re/insurance industry will be forced to rethink traditional approaches to risk modeling, according to Arbol’s Sid Jha, who emphasises that data-driven solutions will play a critical role in managing climate volatility and boosting resilience. “As billions of dollars continue to flow into new infrastructure such as data centers, the industry will be forced to rethink traditional approaches to risk modeling. Jha highlighted the enormous investment opportunities for new infrastructure, particularly through data centres, which are currently undergoing a massive global build-out “The rapid buildout represents a significant growth opportunity for insurers, but the scale and complexity of these facilities also introduce new risks that the industry is still learning to adapt to,” Jha cautioned.

item.title: Inactive Texas Oil and Gas Wells to Go Under Review
item.description: A legislative committee will hear from the Texas Railroad Commission on Tuesday as the agency prepares to update its rules for inactive oil and gas wells, now required under state law. “Our members are always focused on fulfilling our obligations under the law and the regulations that govern active and inactive assets, including requirements related to plugging inactive wells,” said Ben Sheppard, president of the Permian Basin Petroleum Association, regarding the hearing, adding that it is “imperative” that operators shrink the number of inactive wells. It also oversees nearly 160,000 such wells in Texas, and they are at greater risk of becoming orphans, meaning the operator in charge has gone missing or has been bankrupt for at least 12 months.

item.description: The post HCLTech and Keylane partner to fast-track digital transformation of Europe’s life and pension providers appeared first on Insurtech Insights . HCLTech and Keylane Life and Pension, a European provider of SaaS-based core administration platforms for the insurance and pension industry, have announced a partnership to address the modernisation of core IT systems across life insurance and pension services providers in Europe. “With HCLTech’s full-stack portfolio, deep domain expertise and Keylane’s purpose-built platforms, we aim to make these modernization cycles faster and friction free to enable the industry to be ready for the AI-era and deliver digital first experiences to customers.” John Reynders, chief executive officer of Keylane Group, said providers were under increasing pressure to modernise while maintaining continuity.

item.title: Insurance Shopping Has a Missing Layer
item.description: The insurance professional receiving the request may still have to figure out why the person is shopping, whether the request fits, what has already been explained, and what information is still missing. Insurance technology has advanced rapidly, but the critical moment when shopping intent becomes an organized, actionable request remains underdeveloped. That creates work on both sides, and it can make an already confusing insurance-shopping experience feel even more fragmented.
